specCitations: Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:83-86 — a numeral containing only digits has type NaturalNumeral[[n,10,v]] where v is the value of the numeral interpreted in radix ten; nothing bounds v. This is what the wrap violated.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:104-108 — a radix numeral has type NaturalNumeralWithExplicitRadix[[n,r,v]] over the value of its n digits interpreted in radix r. A radix-16 numeral is a natural number, not a bit pattern; this clause decides the second half of the rung.

Specification/basic-lib/basic-integers.tex:368-370 and :398-401 — the wrapping and saturating operators do exactly the same thing as + and - "because operations on type ZZ never need to wrap or saturate"; wrapping has its own spelling and is not what an ordinary operation or coercion does.

Specification/basic/expressions/literals.tex:132-148 — numerals are not directly converted to any number type and Part Library defines coercions from numerals to integers; silent on WHICH number type, which is the reserved fork, tested and not triggered.

Specification/basic/conversions-coercions.tex:40-45 — coercion converts a value of one type to a value of another; nothing licenses truncation, which is consistent with the prelude's own asZZ32 range check and its outOfRange("ZZ32") error.

result.summary:
The branch was relaunched after the container died: commit 7e666704 held the failing test and probes/junit-before.out, and the worktree held uncommitted edits whose last log line showed Integer.test starting and never finishing. Everything was re-run rather than trusted, including javap on the built classes, and the measurements phase B never reached were taken fresh.

Part one is the repair the brief describes. CodeGen.forIntLiteralExpr's bounds become bitLength() <= 31 and <= 63, exact for both signs; FIntLiteral.asNN64 learns to read the decimal string a numeral of bit length 64 now keeps, which was forced and measured (junit-codegen-only.out); asNN32's range check, which masked its argument to 32 bits and so accepted everything, is made to mean what it says, which was a decision and not forced — the brief's premise about asNN32 is corrected in the report.

Part one then turned library_tests/Integer.test from green to four failures, all one thing: a radix numeral whose value is outside the annotated signed type, written to mean a two's-complement bit pattern. literals.tex:104-108 gives such a numeral the value of its digits in its radix, and probes r2g and r2h show the interpreter has always refused the idiom, so these are not correct programs the repair broke — they are programs the language does not accept, on which the two paths now agree. The repair reduces divergence and creates none.

The blast radius was enumerated by value in every radix rather than grepped decimally, which is how the radix-16 half was found. Eighteen lines on the compile path, twelve in range and now right for the right reason, six out of range. Five are repaired: ZZ32_MIN and ZZ64_MIN in the prelude (value-identical, in FortressLibrary.fss:703's spelling), twiceHuge in Integer3 and Integer4 (value-identical, same bit pattern written legally, assertions unchanged), and IntegerChoose2, where 3037000500 is bound at ZZ64 so the test exercises the fast/slow boundary its comment names instead of a negative i. Integer.test is OK (27 tests) again; the rung's own test passes.

The batch's one named stop was tested and is not met: the branch in forIntLiteralExpr chooses an overload of FIntLiteral.make, never a type, every numeral still has the flat static type Types.INT_LITERAL, and r2e and p39 show the arithmetic still happening at IntLiteral — it merely starts from the right operand now. That fork is untouched and still open. Three new ledger rows are owed and named in record.md.
